Reverse order

Write one line with a small gap between characters (up to 16). Hebrew accepts printed and handwritten script letters together, including final letters; digits are also recognized. Normally Hebrew reads right to left and numbers left to right. Reverse the reading order handles an entire line written backwards, including reversed digit sequences. Touching or connected letters may need to be redrawn separately. Automatic word insertion waits at least 2 seconds after the last stroke; turn it off if you need longer.

Starter examples include left/right mirror images for every character. Some shapes become identical, such as b and d. Personal examples help; check uncertain predictions. Mirrored shapes do not automatically reverse the word.

Mirrored starter shapes are bundled locally and contain no child data. Whole-word mode splits and recognizes one line on the device. Word predictions and word corrections are not stored as personal character samples. Guarded Undo may briefly read up to 16 preceding characters to verify that it removes only the text just inserted; that context is not retained or uploaded.
